## Summary
Reviewed the whole package (no diff given): `store.go` (per-tenant file store), `server.go` (HTTP layer), `store_test.go`. No shell tool was available in this session, so `gofmt`/`go vet`/`golangci-lint`/tests could not be run — see Automated Checks.

## Findings

### Must Fix

- [ ] `store.go:78` `path()` guards against escaping the tenant directory with a bare `strings.HasPrefix(p, dir)`.       Evidence: plausible (traced by hand; `TestPathRejectsEscape` only exercises a sibling name (`t2`) that happens not to trigger the bug)
      Fix: compare against `dir` plus the separator, e.g. `if p != dir && !strings.HasPrefix(p, dir+string(filepath.Separator)) { return "", ErrBadName }`.

- [ ] `store.go:100-124` (`Put`) Quota enforcement is check-then-act without holding `s.mu` across the check and the eventual `s.used[tenant] += n`. Two concurrent uploads for the same tenant near the quota boundary can both read a positive `remaining`, both write, and both commit — the tenant ends up stored over quota despite `ErrQuota`'s stated guarantee ("nothing kept... over its quota").
      Evidence: plausible (race traced by hand, not reproduced under `-race`)
      Fix: reserve the bytes atomically before writing (e.g. under `s.mu`, tentatively add `n` to `s.used[tenant]` bounded by `quota`, rolling back if the actual write differs), or serialize per-tenant quota checks with the same lock used for `s.used`.

- [ ] `server.go:257-265` (`encode`) returns `buf.Bytes()` — a slice aliasing the pooled `*bytes.Buffer`'s backing array — while `defer bufPool.Put(buf)` returns that same buffer to the pool as the function returns. A concurrent request can `bufPool.Get()` the same buffer, `Reset()` it, and encode different JSON into the same backing array before `writeJSON` (line 269) calls `w.Write(body)`, corrupting the in-flight response body of the first request.
      Evidence: plausible (classic sync.Pool-returned-slice bug; not reproduced under `-race`/load)
      Fix: copy out before returning, e.g. `return slices.Clone(buf.Bytes()), nil` (or `append([]byte(nil), buf.Bytes()...)`), or write directly to `w` inside the pooled section instead of returning the slice.

- [ ] `server.go:123-127` (`handlePut`) Open-redirect: `next` is accepted whenever `strings.HasPrefix(next, "/")`, which lets `next=//evil.com` through — browsers treat a leading `//` as a protocol-relative absolute URL, so `http.Redirect` sends the client to an attacker-controlled host.
      Evidence: plausible (traced by hand against RFC 3986 / browser behavior for `//host` URLs)
      Fix: reject scheme-relative targets too, e.g. require `strings.HasPrefix(next, "/") && !strings.HasPrefix(next, "//")`.

- [ ] `server.go:150-153` (`handleGet`) Files are served back with the client-supplied `Content-Type` (stored verbatim in `handlePut`, line 117) and no `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. A tenant (or anyone who obtains its token) can upload `Content-Type: text/html` with an HTML/JS body and have it rendered inline by a later viewer's browser on the vault's origin — stored XSS.
      Evidence: plausible (traced by hand)
      Fix: set `w.Header().Set("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")` before writing the body, and/or force `Content-Disposition: attachment` for content types that browsers will render.

# Code Review: `vault` package

## Summary
`Store` persists tenant files on disk with a quota and in-memory metadata cache; `Server` exposes it over HTTP (list/put/get/delete) with bearer-token auth and per-IP upload rate limiting. Reviewed `vault/store.go`, `vault/server.go`, `vault/store_test.go` in full (no diff given, so whole non-test surface).

## Findings

### Must Fix
- [ ] `store.go:48-49` `Meta.ETag()` ranges over `m.Labels`, a Go map, whose iteration order is randomized per call. With two or more labels, `h.Write` sees a different byte order each call, so `ETag()` produces a **different hash for the same `Meta` value from call to call** — directly contradicting the doc comment ("comes out the same on every node") and breaking browser 304 caching for any file with >1 label. `TestETagIsStable` only uses one label, so it doesn't catch this.
  Evidence: plausible (Go spec: map iteration order is unspecified/randomized; traced the code path).
  Fix: sort the label keys before hashing, e.g. `for _, k := range slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(m.Labels)) { h.Write(...) }`.

- [ ] `store.go:78` `path()`'s containment check `strings.HasPrefix(p, dir)` is a bare string-prefix test with no separator boundary. A tenant `t1` can reach tenant `t10`'s directory: `dir = root/t1`, and `name = "../t10/secret.txt"` cleans to `p = root/t10/secret.txt`, which has `root/t1` as a *string* prefix and so passes. This breaks tenant isolation, the core security property of the package.
  Evidence: plausible (traced `filepath.Join`/`Clean` semantics; the existing test `TestPathRejectsEscape` only exercises a case where the prefix genuinely differs, so it doesn't catch this).
  Fix: `if p != dir && !strings.HasPrefix(p, dir+string(filepath.Separator)) { return "", ErrBadName }`.

- [ ] `store.go:162-174` `Delete` removes the file and its metadata entry but never decrements `s.used[tenant]`. Every delete permanently leaks quota: a tenant that uploads and deletes files repeatedly eventually hits `ErrQuota` while owning zero bytes on disk.
  Evidence: verified (read `Delete` end-to-end; `s.used` is written only in `Put`, at line 128, and read in `remaining`/`Used`, never decremented elsewhere).
  Fix: under the same lock, `if m, ok := s.files[tenant][name]; ok { s.used[tenant] -= m.Size }` before/while deleting the map entry.

- [ ] `store.go:100-134` `Put` checks `remaining(tenant)` (locks, reads, unlocks) and only locks again *after* the disk write completes to update `s.used`. Two concurrent uploads for the same tenant near the quota boundary can both pass the check and both succeed, taking the tenant over quota — the documented invariant ("nothing kept... when the file would take the tenant over its quota") does not hold under concurrency, which `Store`'s own mutex implies it's designed for.
  Evidence: plausible (race traced by inspection; no test exercises concurrent `Put`).
  Fix: reserve the byte budget atomically before writing (e.g. hold `s.mu` across a check-and-reserve step, or use an atomic "used += n, roll back on failure" pattern) rather than check-then-write-then-commit.

### Should Fix
- [ ] `server.go:78` `WriteTimeout: 10 * time.Second` on a server that accepts uploads up to `maxUpload` (256 MiB, `server.go:20`) and serves arbitrarily large files back out. A legitimate large upload/download over a slow-to-average connection will be killed mid-transfer once the 10s budget (which covers the whole request lifecycle, not just headers) expires.
  Evidence: plausible (go-http skill: "`WriteTimeout` exceeds the slowest handler").
  Fix: drop `WriteTimeout` (rely on `ReadHeaderTimeout` + per-request deadlines via `http.NewResponseController`) or size it generously relative to `maxUpload` at the slowest expected throughput.

- [ ] `server.go:222-224` `clientIP` trusts `X-Forwarded-For` unconditionally from any client, with no check that the request actually came through a trusted proxy. Since this value is the key for `allowUpload`'s per-minute rate limit, any client can set an arbitrary `X-Forwarded-For` on each request and bypass the upload rate limit entirely.
  Evidence: plausible (read the header handling; no proxy allowlist or `RemoteAddr` trust check present anywhere in the file).
  Fix: only honor `X-Forwarded-For` when `r.RemoteAddr` is a configured trusted proxy; otherwise use `r.RemoteAddr` directly.

- [ ] `store.go:72-82` `path()` validates `name` against traversal via the prefix check but never validates `tenant` itself (only rejects empty). `Store` is a public API usable outside the HTTP layer (whose `ServeMux` happens to clean `..` segments before routing), so a direct caller passing `tenant = ".."` or a tenant containing `/` escapes the intended root entirely. The store shouldn't rely on an HTTP-layer side effect for its own safety invariant.
  Evidence: plausible (traced `filepath.Join(s.root, tenant)`, which itself calls `Clean`, so `tenant=".."` yields the parent of `root`).
  Fix: reject `tenant` containing `/`, `\`, or resolving outside `root` the same way `name` is checked.

- [ ] `store.go:38` `Meta.Expires` is defined and serialized (`json:"expires,omitzero"`) but nothing in the package ever sets it (no server field for it) or enforces it (`Open`/`List` never check it, no reaper). It's a documented-looking feature that doesn't work.
  Evidence: verified (grepped both files; `Expires` appears only in the struct tag and the doc comment for `Meta`).
  Fix: either wire it up (reject/purge expired files in `Open`/`List`, add a way to set it) or remove the field until it's implemented.

- [ ] Test gap: add a test for the sibling-tenant prefix bug (`t1` vs `t10`) and for `ETag()` stability with ≥2 labels — both Must Fix bugs above would have been caught by the existing suite's pattern if it covered these cases.
  Fix: extend `TestPathRejectsEscape` and `TestETagIsStable` with these cases.

### Nits
- [ ] `store.go:114` `io.LimitReader(r, remaining+1)` overflows if `remaining` is `math.MaxInt64` (only reachable with an extreme configured quota); effectively theoretical but worth a comment or a `min`/guard if quotas are ever caller-configurable to arbitrary values.
- [ ] `server.go:165-169` `handleDelete` records a `"delete"` audit event even when the named file never existed (`Store.Delete` is documented as a no-op for a missing name), which can make the audit trail look like data was removed when it wasn't.

## Review: `worker` package (`pool.go`, `pool_test.go`)

**Automated checks:** unavailable — no shell/lint tool accessible in this session; gofmt/go vet/golangci-lint were not run. Findings below are from manual reading, each marked `verified` (traced through code) or `plausible`.

### Must Fix

1. **pool.go:66** — `verified`. `Snapshot`'s copy is a no-op:
   ```go
   out := make([]error, 0, len(p.failed))
   copy(out, p.failed)
   ```
   `copy` copies `min(len(dst), len(src))` elements, and `out` has length 0, so nothing is ever copied — `Snapshot()` always returns an empty slice. Fix: `out := make([]error, len(p.failed)); copy(out, p.failed)` (or `append([]error(nil), p.failed...)`).

2. **pool.go:38-44** — `verified`. When `p.ctx` is cancelled mid-loop, `Run` returns immediately (line 39), but goroutines already spawned for earlier jobs are still executing and will block forever on `errs <- job(p.ctx)` (line 43) because nothing ever drains `errs` again — it's unbuffered and no one selects on it after the early return. Every in-flight job goroutine leaks permanently. Fix: make the send cancellation-aware too (e.g. `select { case errs <- job(p.ctx): case <-p.ctx.Done(): }`), or drain remaining results with a ctx-aware select before returning.

3. **pool.go:47-49 vs. 56-59, 63-68** — `verified`. `Run` appends to `p.failed` (line 48) without holding `p.mu`, while `Failed()`/`Snapshot()` read `p.failed` under `p.mu`. Calling `Failed()`/`Snapshot()` concurrently with an in-progress `Run` (a reasonable use — polling progress) is a data race. Fix: take `p.mu` around the append in `Run`.

4. **pool.go:104** — `verified`. `SessionToken` builds a bearer token the partner "trusts... for an hour" using `math/rand`, which is not cryptographically secure and is predictable if the generator's state is inferred from other output. A forgeable session token is a real auth weakness. Fix: generate the bytes with `crypto/rand` and hex-encode them.

5. **pool.go:19, 26, 32** — `verified`. `ctx` is stored on `Pool` instead of being a parameter to `Run`. This violates the standard Go convention (context as first parameter, never in a struct) and has a real consequence here: a `Pool` is permanently bound to the context it was constructed with, so it can't be reused with a fresh context, and a caller has no way to run the same pool with a different deadline/cancellation per call. Fix: drop the `ctx` field; add `ctx context.Context` as `Run`'s first parameter.

### Should Fix

6. **pool.go:97** — `verified`. `fmt.Errorf("after %d attempts: %v", attempts, err)` uses `%v`, discarding the error chain, so callers can't `errors.Is`/`errors.As` the underlying failure. Fix: use `%w`.

7. **pool.go:34** — `plausible`. `sem := make(chan struct{}, p.Workers)`: if `Workers <= 0` (easy to hit via `&Pool{}` or `New(ctx, 0)`), the channel has capacity 0, so the very first `sem <- struct{}{}` (line 37) blocks forever with no goroutine yet running to drain it — `Run` hangs indefinitely unless `ctx` happens to already be cancelled. Fix: validate `Workers >= 1` in `New` (return an error, clamp to 1, or panic with a clear message).

8. **pool.go:86-98** — `plausible`. `Retry`'s backoff (`time.Sleep`, line 91) ignores context cancellation — even if `ctx` is cancelled between attempts, `Retry` keeps sleeping and retrying rather than returning promptly. Fix: replace the bare sleep with a `select` on a timer and `ctx.Done()`.

9. **pool_test.go:18** — `verified`. `time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)` right after `p.Run(jobs)` synchronizes nothing — `Run` already blocks until it has collected a result for every job — so this just pads the test with a fixed delay for no reason (and violates the "no sleep-based waits" convention). Fix: delete the line.

### Nits

10. **pool.go:22** — `seen map[string]bool` is used purely as a set (`p.seen[key] = true`, never read for `false` vs. missing distinction beyond truthiness). `map[string]struct{}` better expresses set semantics and avoids the bool storage.

11. **pool.go:18** — exported field `Workers` has no doc comment of its own; only the `Pool` type comment mentions it. Minor, since the type comment already documents its role.

### Summary
Two independent correctness bugs (broken `Snapshot`, goroutine leak on cancellation) and a data race make this package unsafe for concurrent/robust use as written; the stored-context design and the weak `SessionToken` source are also worth fixing before merge.

# Code Review: `partner` package

## Summary
Client for a fulfillment partner's HTTP API with rate limiting and circuit breaking. No automated checks were run — no shell tool is available in this session, so gofmt/vet/build/test/lint results are all `unavailable (no shell)`. This review is static reading only.

## Findings

### Must Fix

- [ ] **client.go:102-110** Retried request body goes stale. `body` is marshaled once and wrapped in a single `bytes.Reader` (`payload`) that is reused across every retry attempt inside the `for attempt := range c.attempts` loop. `io.Reader` state is consumed on the first attempt; every retry after that sends an empty body, since the reader is already at EOF.
      Evidence: plausible (read; `bytes.Reader`'s position advances on `Read` and is never reset between loop iterations)
      Fix: build a fresh `bytes.NewReader(body)` inside the loop (or set `req.GetBody` and call it) before each attempt.

- [ ] **client.go:146** `Idempotency-Key` is generated inside `try`, which runs once per retry attempt, so each retry of the same `Submit` call gets a different key. This directly contradicts the doc comment on `Submit` ("the partner deduplicates on the Idempotency-Key header, so a retried submission never creates a second shipment") and can create duplicate shipments on retry.

If `fn` calls `p.Failed()`, `p.Snapshot()`, or another `Once`-wrapped job on the same pool, it deadlocks on the non-reentrant `sync.Mutex`.       Evidence: plausible (read; `sync.Mutex` is not reentrant)

**store.go:162-174 — `Delete` never decrements `s.used[tenant]`, `verified`**

```go
	...
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	delete(s.files[tenant], name)
	return nil

```
The file is removed from disk and from `s.files`, but `s.used[tenant]` is never reduced. Every delete permanently shrinks the tenant's effective quota (`remaining` at store.go:85-89 uses `s.used`), eventually locking the tenant out even with no files stored.

**store.go:85-89, 100-134 — quota check has a TOCTOU race, `verified`**

## Findings

### Must Fix

- [ ] [store.go:78] `path()`'s traversal check, `!strings.HasPrefix(p, dir)`, is a plain string prefix test with no separator boundary. A tenant `t1` has `dir = "<root>/t1"`; a name like `../t1-evil/secret` cleans to `<root>/t1-evil/secret`, which still has `<root>/t1` as a string prefix, so the check passes and the file is written/read/deleted outside `t1`'s directory, breaking tenant isolation.
      Evidence: plausible (traced `filepath.Join`/`filepath.Clean` semantics by hand; not executed)
      Fix: `if p != dir && !strings.HasPrefix(p, dir+string(filepath.Separator)) { return "", ErrBadName }`.

- [ ] [store.go:46-51] `ETag()` ranges directly over `m.Labels` (`for k, v := range m.Labels`) and streams each pair into the hash in iteration order. Go map iteration order is randomized per range, so the same `Meta` with ≥2 labels can hash to different ETags on different calls/nodes, contradicting the doc comment "comes out the same on every node" — clients get spurious 200s instead of 304s, and cross-node ETag comparisons become unreliable.
      Evidence: plausible (Go map iteration order is documented as unspecified/randomized; `TestETagIsStable` only exercises a single-label map, so it wouldn't catch this)
      Fix: iterate a sorted key list, e.g. `for _, k := range slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(m.Labels)) { h.Write(...) }`.

- [ ] [store.go:162-174] `Delete` removes the file from disk and from `s.files[tenant]` but never subtracts the file's size from `s.used[tenant]`. Quota consumption is permanent even after deletion, so `Used()` over-reports usage and a tenant that deletes and re-uploads will eventually be denied uploads (`ErrQuota`) despite being well under real usage.
      Evidence: verified (read against `TestDeleteRemovesFile`, which never asserts `Used()` after delete, so the gap is untested)
      Fix: before deleting, look up the existing `Meta` (or capture its `Size`) and do `s.used[tenant] -= m.Size` under the same lock, floored at 0.

- [ ] [server.go:219-230] `clientIP` trusts the first (leftmost) hop of the client-supplied `X-Forwarded-For` header to key the per-address rate limiter in `allowUpload`. The leftmost XFF entry is the value the client itself claims, so any caller can set an arbitrary or rotating fake address to bypass `uploadsPerMinute` entirely, or spoof another client's address to make it look like *they* are being rate-limited.
      Evidence: plausible (standard XFF spoofing; no proxy validation exists in this code path)
      Fix: only honor `X-Forwarded-For` when the immediate peer is a configured trusted proxy, and then use the proxy-appended (rightmost trusted) hop, not the client-supplied leftmost one; otherwise key on `r.RemoteAddr` alone.

  Evidence: plausible (read)
